implementation_notes: Hanami is the closest Ruby framework to ADR's per-request unit: config/routes.rb maps each route to one action class under app/actions, and #handle(request, response) receives Rack request/response objects. Hanami does not require a separate Responder class - the response object is the transport responder - so delegate business work to an interactor or service and extract serializer or response policy when it grows. Choose Hanami when you want one action class per route; choose Sinatra or Rails when the framework's own controller model is already acceptable.
code_sketch:
# app/actions/users/show.rb
module Users
  class Show < Bookshelf::Action                 # Hanami::Action
    def handle(request, response)
      user = user_repo.find(request.params[:id])          # domain
      response.status = user ? 200 : 404
      response.body   = user ? UserSerializer.new(user).to_json : "" # responder
    end
  end
end
pitfalls: Action instances are reused across requests: instance variables assigned in #handle leak between requests and race under threaded servers.
A new action file that is not reachable through the router fails at boot rather than at request time, which surprises teams used to implicit routing.
Building the response inside the interactor re-couples presentation to business logic; keep formatting in the responder.

variants.name: Sinatra route block whose return value is the body
variants.idiom_name: Sinatra route block with params and return value
variants.implementation_notes: Sinatra expresses the same boundary with less structure: a get '/users/:id' do ... end block is the Action and its return value - or an explicit body/halt call - is the response, with params as collected input. JSON is not a core route helper, so require Sinatra::JSON or use JSON.generate and set content_type explicitly. It needs no class per endpoint, but it has no responder object by default, so multi-format endpoints can drift into branching inside the block; move to Hanami or an explicit responder when response building grows.
variants.code_sketch:
require "json"
get '/users/:id' do                       # action
  user = UserRepo.find(params[:id])       # domain
  halt 404 unless user
  content_type :json                      # responder
  JSON.generate(id: user.id, name: user.name)
end
pitfalls: halt aborts the route immediately: code after it never runs, so a helper that halts after partially setting a response can leave a misleading status or body -> decide the complete error response before halting.

Sinatra creates a new app instance for each request, but class-scope settings and class variables are shared: storing request data there leaks between requests -> keep it in locals or request-scoped state.
Sinatra's default routing is first-match: a catch-all route defined early shadows later, more specific routes -> order specific routes before fallbacks.
